Poem of Gilgameš – Standard Babylonian III: “‘[Come Back In Safety] To [The Quay Of] Uruk!”

  • Source: eBL corpus – https://www.ebl.lmu.de/corpus/L/1/4/Standard%20Babylonian/III
  • API: https://www.ebl.lmu.de/api/texts/L/1/4/chapters/Standard%20Babylonian/III/display
  • Edition: Andrew R. George (editor); Geraldina Rozzi (revision); Enrique Jiménez (revision)
  • Translation: Andrew R. George; Anmar A. Fadhil; Wasim Khatabe
  • Generated by tools/ebl_fetch.py on 2026-10-17 – do not edit by hand; re-run the tool instead.

Per line: N = normalized Akkadian reconstruction (| metrical foot, || caesura); T = eBL English translation; L = lemmas with eBL dictionary glosses; then notes, parallel lines, and the manuscripts' transliterations (ATF). Bibliography keys like [RN117: 889] are resolved in bibliography.md (RN117 = George 2003).

1

  • N: [ana kāri | ša] uruk || [ṭihâ | ina šulmi]
  • T: ‘[Come back in safety] to [the quay of] Uruk!
  • L: [ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; kāri ← kāru I “quay, port”; ša] ← ša I “who(m), which”; uruk ← Uruk I; [ṭihâ ← ṭehû I “to be(come) near to, approach”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; šulmi] ← šulmu I “completeness”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "III" 215; L I.4 SB "III" 215
NinNA1b i 1. [a]-na# [ka-a-ri ša₂] UNUG#{ki#} [ṭi-ha-a ina šul-mi]

2

  • N: [l]ā tatakkil | gilgāmeš || ana gimir (|) emūqīka
  • T: Do not trust, O Gilgameš, in the fullness of your strength,
  • L: [l]ā ← lā I “not, no”; tatakkil ← takālu I “to trust (in = ana, -iš, dat.)”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; gimir ← gimru I “totality”; emūqīka ← emūqu I “pl. m. & f. strength”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "III" 249; L I.4 SB "III" 216
NinNA2c i 2. [x x x x x x x x x x x x] e#-mu#-[qi₂-ka]
NinNA1b i 2. [l]a ta-tak-kil {d#}GIŠ#-gim₂-maš a-na gi#-mir# e-mu#-qi₂#-ka#

3

  • N: [ī]nāka | lišbâ || mihiṣka | tukkil
  • T: let your eyes be satisfied, strike a blow to rely on!
  • L: [ī]nāka ← īnu I “f. eye”; lišbâ ← šebû I “to be full (of = acc.)”; mihiṣka ← mihiṣtu I “pl. mihṣātu, NB also mihilētu strike M/NB”; tukkil ← takālu I “to trust (in = ana, -iš, dat.)”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 OB "III" 250; L I.4 SB "III" 217; cf. L I.4 SB "V" 137
NinNA2c i 3. [x x x x x x mi-hi-i]ṣ-ka tuk-[kil]
NinNA1b i 3. [i]-na-ka liš-ba-a mi-hi-iṣ-ka tuk-k[il]

4

  • N: ālik (|) mahri || tappâ | ušezz[eb]
  • T: “He who goes in front saves (his) comrade,
  • L: ālik ← alāku I “to go”; mahri ← mahru II “front”; tappâ ← tappû I “companion, partner friend”; ušezz[eb] ← ezēbu I “to leave, leave behind”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "III" 255; L I.4 SB "III" 218
NinNA2c i 4. [x x x x tap-p]a-a u₂-še-e[z-zeb]
NinNA1b i 4. a#-lik mah-ri TAB.BA-a u₂-še-ez-z[eb]

5

  • N: ša ṭūda | īdû || ibiršu | iṣṣur
  • T: he who knew the road protected his friend.”
  • L: ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; ṭūda ← ṭūdu I “f. & m. way, path Bab.(lit.), NA? ṭ. ṣabātu to take a road”; īdû ← edû II “to know (M/NA cf. wadûm)”; ibiršu ← ibru I “friend, colleague”; iṣṣur ← naṣāru I “to guard, protect”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "III" 256; L I.4 SB "III" 219; cf. L I.4 SB "III" 135
NinNA2c i 5. [x x x x x x] i#-bir-šu iṣ-ṣur#
NinNA1b i 5. ša₂ ṭu₂-du i-du-u₂ i-bir-šu₂ iṣ-ṣu[r]

6

  • N: [l]illik | enkīdu | ina pānīka
  • T: Let Enkidu go in front of you,
  • L: [l]illik ← alāku I “to go”; enkīdu ← Enkidu I; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; pānīka ← pānu I “front, pl. face”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "III" 251; L I.4 SB "III" 77; L I.4 SB "III" 220
NinNA2c i 6. [x x x x x] i-na pa-ni-ka
NinNA1b i 6. [l]il-lik {d}+en-ki-du₃ i-na pa-ni-k[a]

7

  • N: īde | harrāna || ša qišti (|) erēni
  • T: he knows the way to the Forest of Cedar!
  • L: īde ← edû II “to know (M/NA cf. wadûm)”; harrāna ← harrānu I “f., later also m. way, road”; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; qišti ← qištu I “pl. qišātu(m) forest, wood q. erēnim cedar forest”; erēni ← erēnu I “cedar OAkk qišti e. cedar forest”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "III" 78; L I.4 SB "III" 221

8

  • N: [t]āhāza | amir-ma || qabla | kullum
  • T: He is tried in battles and experienced in combat,
  • L: [t]āhāza ← tāhāzu I “pl. f. battle”; amir-ma ← amāru I “to see”; qabla ← qablu II “f. & m. battle q. epēšu to do battle”; kullum ← kullumu I
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "III" 252; L I.4 SB "III" 222

NinNA1b i 8. [t]a-ha-zi a-mir-ma qab-lu kul-l[um]

9

  • N: enkīdu (|) ibra | liṣṣur || tappâ | lišallim
  • T: let Enkidu protect (his) friend and keep safe (his) comrade!
  • L: enkīdu ← Enkidu I; ibra ← ibru I “friend, colleague”; liṣṣur ← naṣāru I “to guard, protect”; tappâ ← tappû I “companion, partner friend”; lišallim ← šalāmu I “(as subst.)”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "III" 224

NinNA1b i 9. {d}+en-ki-du₃ ib-ri li-iṣ-ṣur tap-pa-a li-šal-li[m]

10

  • N: ana ṣēr (|) hīrāti || pagaršu | libla
  • T: let him bring his person back to his wives!
  • L: ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; ṣēr ← ṣēru I “back, upperside”; hīrāti ← hīrtu I “(equal ranking) wife Bab. of humans, deities”; pagaršu ← pagru I “pl. pagrū, jB also f., NB also pagrānu body”; libla ← wabālu I “(cf. also babālu) to carry, bring”

  • N: ina puhrīnī-ma | nipqidakka | šarra
  • T: In this our assembly we hereby give the king into your care:
  • L: ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; puhrīnī-ma ← puhru I “pl. f. assembly”; nipqidakka ← paqādu I “to entrust”; šarra ← šarru I “pl. šarrū, šarrānu king”

  • Note: See [RN117: 814]: “The reference to mules is to the steeds that pull the sun’s chariot through the sky. They are also known from a line of an incantation in Bīt rimki: ta-(aṣ)-ṣa-an-da pa-re-ka (var. gir₃{meš}) ša₂ šit-mu-ru la-sa-[ma] (var. a-la-kam), ‘you (Šamaš) have hitched up your mules, which are ardent for running’ (cf. [RN2801: 57, 63]).” On the team of Šamaš’s chariot, see also [RN765]. See also [fromebllab0039: 105]: “ḫarāpu Š means “to cause someone to be early at something”, as in the Hymn to Ninurta as Savior l. 2: lā tēbâ tušaḫrap urḫa, “Early you set on his way him who else would not rise” ([RN358]; @url{/corpus/L/3/10}{eBL Corpus L III.10}). The context here suggests understanding the verb as a reference to an early sunset, rather than to dawn (cf. [RN117: 460]). Alternatively, one may restore the verb as erēbu Š, “to set”, although the sign before ri is not še.”
